v.q: How do Spring, Spring Boot and Spring MVC relate?
o: Spring is the core framework, MVC is its web module, and Boot configures them automatically
Spring Boot is the core and Spring MVC and Spring Framework are plugins for it
Spring MVC replaced Spring when Boot was released and is now the only web stack
They are three separate products that cannot be combined in one project
v.w: The Framework is the foundation (container, AOP, transactions, MVC and WebFlux). MVC is one of its modules. Boot is a convenience layer on top: starters, auto-configuration, embedded server.

v.q: Which statement about Spring, Boot and MVC is NOT true?
o: Spring Boot replaced the Spring Framework
Spring MVC is a web module
Boot adds auto-configuration
Boot builds on the Spring Framework
v.w: Boot is built on the framework. It does not replace it.

v.q: What is the relationship between JPA, Hibernate and Spring Data JPA?
o: JPA is the API, Hibernate implements it, and Spring Data JPA generates repositories on top
Hibernate is the API, JPA implements it, and Spring Data JPA replaces both
Spring Data JPA is the API, Hibernate implements it, and JPA generates repositories
They are three names for the same library released in different years
v.w: Spring Data JPA, then JPA (specification), then Hibernate (provider), then JDBC, then the database.

v.q: Which layer of the stack is the API specification only?
o: JPA
Hibernate
Spring Data JPA
JDBC driver
v.w: JPA defines annotations and interfaces. Hibernate is one implementation of it.

v.q: What is a bean in Spring?
o: An object created, wired and managed by the Spring container
Any Java class with a public constructor and getters
A configuration file that defines the application properties
A thread that handles one HTTP request at a time
v.w: Beans are the objects the ApplicationContext creates from definitions, injects with dependencies and can wrap in proxies.

v.q: Which object is a Spring bean?
o: One the container manages
Any class with a getter method
Any object created with new
Any thread in the JVM
v.w: Beans are the objects the container wires together.

v.q: Which Spring feature adds transactions, caching and security checks around your methods without editing them?
o: AOP, implemented with proxies
Component scanning, implemented with reflection
Auto-configuration, implemented with starters
Profiles, implemented with environment properties
v.w: AOP wraps beans in proxies that run extra behaviour before and after the call. That is also why self-invocation inside a class bypasses these annotations.

v.q: Which feature is NOT implemented with proxies?
o: Component scanning
@Transactional
@Cacheable
Method security
v.w: Component scanning finds classes at startup. The others wrap method calls.

v.q: What does Spring Boot auto-configuration do?
o: Creates default beans from the classpath and properties, backing off when you define your own
Rewrites your source code at build time to add missing annotations
Downloads and installs an application server on the host machine
Scans the database schema and generates entity classes at start-up
v.w: Auto-configuration is conditional: it registers sensible beans (DataSource, Jackson, embedded Tomcat) and is skipped when you provide your own.

v.q: Which statement about auto-configuration is NOT true?
o: It overrides beans you define yourself
It reacts to the classpath
It reads properties
It backs off when you define a bean
v.w: Conditional rules let your own bean win.

v.q: What does Spring Data's repository interface give you?
o: Generated implementation of CRUD, paging and derived queries from the interface alone
A full SQL migration tool that versions the database schema
A load balancer that spreads queries over several database nodes
An HTTP client for calling other services
v.w: You write an interface such as JpaRepository<Account, Long> and Spring Data creates the implementation at start-up. Schema migration is Flyway or Liquibase.

v.q: Which method name is a valid derived query in Spring Data?
o: findByEmail
fetchMeTheEmail
queryEmails
emailQuery
v.w: The prefix find...By followed by a property name is parsed into a query.

v.q: When is Spring Batch a better choice than a @Scheduled method?
o: Processing millions of records with chunking, restart and skip rules
Running a tiny cleanup once an hour on a single instance
Calling a REST endpoint with a retry whenever a user logs in
Publishing a Spring application event to another bean
v.w: @Scheduled only triggers code. Batch adds chunked transactions, restart from failure, skip and retry policy, and job history for large jobs.

o: A nightly bulk import
A tiny hourly cleanup
A single REST call
A UI event handler
v.w: Batch brings chunking, restart and skip rules for big jobs.

v.q: Where does Spring Security run in a servlet application?
o: In a filter chain in front of the DispatcherServlet
Inside each controller method as an explicit call you write
In the database driver as a login plugin
Only at start-up, when the beans are created
v.w: The SecurityFilterChain authenticates and authorises before the DispatcherServlet and your controller see the request. Method security adds checks deeper in.

v.q: Which component sits in front of the DispatcherServlet for security?
o: The security filter chain
The repository
The view resolver
The JPA entity
v.w: Filters run before the servlet, so a rejected request never reaches the controller.
